wikitext: {{EpicodePrevNext| prevcode=PG02 | prevtitle=The Chase | nextcode=PG04 | nexttitle=The Lake of Rage | series=Pokémon Generations | colorscheme=Hoso}} {{EpisodeInfobox| epcode=PG03 | colorscheme=Hoso| title_en=The Challenger | title_ja=挑戦者 | title_ja_trans=The Challenger | release_method=Web release | screen=hd | broadcast_jp=December 9, 2016| broadcast_us=September 23, 2016 | en_op=N/A | ja_op=N/A | ja_ed=N/A | olmteam=Team Kato | scenario=冨岡淳広 | storyboard=冨安大貴 | director=傳沙織 | art=海島千本 | morecredits=no | epstaffpage=PG01-PG10 | footnotes=* ''[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ktskEn5q7gg The Challenger]'' on the official English Pokémon [[YouTube]] channel. * {{BMGf|218552|Review thread on BMGf}} }} '''The Challenger''' (Japanese: '''挑戦者''' ''The Challenger'') is the third episode of [[Pokémon Generations]]. It was first released on the official English Pokémon [[YouTube]] channel on September 23, 2016. It was uploaded to the official Japanese Pokémon [[YouTube]] channel on December 9, 2016. {{spoilers}} ==Blurb== A new challenger approaches to test his abilities against the Kanto region’s Elite Four. Will he prove himself worthy? ==Plot== At [[Indigo Plateau]], the members of the [[Kanto]] [[Elite Four]], [[Lance]], [[Bruno]], [[Lorelei]], and [[Agatha]], emerge from their personal chambers. They prepare to take their positions for a new challenger, who has managed to collect eight [[Gym]] [[Badge]]s, a feat that hasn't been seen in a long time. Lorelei gloats to Agatha that she'll defeat the challenger before her, while Bruno cracks his knuckles and grins. Lance tells everyone to prepare themselves, looking forward to seeing how strong the challenger will be. As the Elite Four members take their places in their respective rooms, outside the Pokémon League, the challenger, {{ga|Blue}}, approaches the building, proclaiming himself to be the greatest [[Pokémon Trainer]] in the {{pkmn|world}}. Blue enters Lorelei's room, where the {{type|Ice}} [[Type expert|expert]] welcomes him to the Pokémon League. The {{pkmn|battle}} advances, with Blue's {{p|Alakazam}} eventually facing Lorelei's {{p|Lapras}}. The [[Pokémon category|Transport Pokémon]] attempts to use {{m|Body Slam}}, but the Psi Pokémon easily dodges the attack with {{m|Teleport}}. As Lapras frantically tries to locate its opponent, it suddenly gets lifted into air by a {{m|Psychic}} attack, soon sending the bulky Pokémon hurtling into the floor and defeating it. Blue gloats about his geniusness as Lorelei reluctantly lets him move forward. Next, Blue faces Bruno. The {{type|Fighting}} expert tells Blue to show him his Pokémon, before letting out a roar of determination. Unfazed, Blue hopes Bruno to give him at least a bit more of a challenge. The battle commences, finally leading to Blue's {{p|Pidgeot}} confronting Bruno's {{p|Machamp}}. The Superpower Pokémon does its best to block Pidgeot's {{m|Wing Attack}}, but the {{DL|Type|Type effectiveness|super effective}} attack quickly overpowers Machamp, sending it flying straight into Bruno and both of them into the wall. Bruno is shocked by his loss as Blue walks past him towards the next room, scoffing at the lack of challenge and gloating that he and his Pokémon haven't even nearly gotten serious yet. Now facing up against the {{type|Ghost}} expert Agatha, Blue defeats her {{p|Arbok}} with his {{p|Rhydon}}. [[Recall]]ing her defeated Pokémon, Agatha compliments on Blue's skills. Blue says that everything is going according to his plan, and Agatha admits that since he's the grandson of "[[Professor Oak|that old coot]]", she had thought he'd focus on completing the [[Pokédex]]. Blue angrily snaps at Agatha not to compare him to his grandfather, saying that for him, gathering data for the Pokédex is just a tool to become stronger. Opening the {{i|Poké Ball}} embedded on her walking stick, Agatha calls out her last Pokémon, {{TP|Agatha|Gengar}}. Moving on to the final room, Blue now comes face to face with the leader of the Elite Four, Lance, declaring that he'll defeat him and claim himself the {{pkmn|Champion}} throne. Starting the battle, the {{type|Dragon}} master calls out his {{TP|Lance|Dragonite}}, while Blue sends out his {{p|Blastoise}}. Both Pokémon attack simultaneously, Dragonite with {{m|Flamethrower}} and Blastoise with {{m|Hydro Pump}}. Both [[Move|attacks]] score direct hits, with Lance complimenting the power of Blastoise's attack. Determined to finish the battle, Blue has Blastoise continue the assault with {{m|Skull Bash}}, and Lance responds in kind, with the two Pokémon clashing in the middle of the battlefield. In the dark, unlit Champion's room, Blue is now sitting on a throne, having finally claimed himself the title of Pokémon League Champion. However, another person soon walks into the room, which Blue had been expecting. As the person enters and the room lights up, Blue stands up from his throne, welcoming his rival {{ga|Red}}. ==Major events== * {{ga|Blue}} challenges the [[Elite Four]] of [[Kanto]] and defeats them, becoming {{pkmn|Champion}}. * {{ga|Red}}, having defeated the Elite Four as well, prepares to start his {{pkmn|battle}} with Blue for the title of Champion. ==Characters== ===Humans=== * {{ga|Red}} * {{ga|Blue}} * [[Lorelei]] * [[Bruno]] * [[Agatha]] * [[Lance]] ===Pokémon=== * {{p|Alakazam}} ({{ga|Blue}}'s) * {{p|Pidgeot}} ({{ga|Blue}}'s) * {{p|Rhydon}} ({{ga|Blue}}'s) * {{p|Blastoise}} ({{ga|Blue}}'s) * {{p|Lapras}} ([[Lorelei]]'s) * {{p|Machamp}} ([[Bruno]]'s) * {{p|Arbok}} ([[Agatha]]'s) * {{p|Gengar}} ({{OP|Agatha|Gengar}}) * {{p|Dragonite}} ({{OP|Lance|Dragonite}}) ==Trivia== * {{ga|Blue}} is revealed to own {{p|Blastoise}}, the fully evolved [[first partner Pokémon]] that has a type disadvantage to {{ga|Red}}'s {{p|Bulbasaur}}. In all other media, Blue always has the first partner Pokémon that has the type advantage to Red's. * This episode was shown in US theaters alongside ''[[M20|I Choose You!]]''. ===Errors=== * When Blue's {{p|Pidgeot}} uses {{m|Wing Attack}} and hits [[Bruno]]'s {{p|Machamp}}, its wings glow, but when the shot moves on to show Machamp being sent flying into Bruno, the wings are no longer glowing. ==In other languages== {{Epilang|color=FDBB99|bordercolor=FD7F4F |nl={{tt|De uitdager|The challenger}} |fr_eu={{tt|Le challenger|The challenger}} |de={{tt|Der Herausforderer|The Challenger}} |it={{tt|Lo sfidante|The challenger}} |ko={{tt|도전자|The Challenger}} |pt_br={{tt|O Desafiante|The Challenger}} |es_eu={{tt|El aspirante|The challenger}} }} {{-}} {{EpicodePrevNext| prevcode=PG02 | prevtitle=The Chase | nextcode=PG04 | nexttitle=The Lake of Rage | series=Pokémon Generations | colorscheme=Hoso}} {{Project Anime notice}} [[Category:Pokémon Generations episodes|03]] [[Category:Episodes written by Atsuhiro Tomioka]] [[Category:Episodes storyboarded by Daiki Tomiyasu]] [[Category:Episodes directed by Saori Den]] [[Category:Episodes animated by Senbon Umishima]] [[Category:Episodes which aired in the United States before Japan]] [[de:Pokémon Generationen Folge 3: Der Herausforderer]] [[es:GEN03]] [[fr:PG03]] [[it:PG03]] [[ja:PG第3話]] [[zh:宝可梦世代 第3集]]
